# Webflow Bridge

> A local bridge that drives the browser tab you already have open and logged in — local only, no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

## What this is

Webflow Bridge is a small Python daemon on your machine plus a Chrome/Edge extension (and a separate Firefox edition). Your scripts and AI agents POST JSON commands to the daemon, which drives the real, already-logged-in tab: your session, your cookies, your page state. Everything stays on your machine. The daemon is pure Python stdlib, binds to `127.0.0.1`, and needs no account, no cloud and no API key.

## Install (shortest path)

1. Start the daemon from the repo root: `python3 daemon/webflow_bridge.py` (Windows: `py -3.11 daemon/webflow_bridge.py`).
2. Load the `extension/` folder once at `chrome://extensions` or `edge://extensions` (Developer mode, Load unpacked). This manual step is the only one that needs a human.
3. Point your scripts at `http://127.0.0.1:10086`. Full detail: `docs/INSTALL.md`.

## Local HTTP contract

- Base URL: `http://127.0.0.1:10086`
- Endpoint: `POST /command` with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`
- Auth: the shared token file at `~/.webflow_bridge/token`, sent on every request as an `Authorization: Bearer` header
- Body: `{"action": ..., "args": {...}, "session": "default"}` — the daemon answers `session` only as `"default"`
- Success is `{"status": "ok", "data": {"value": ...}}`; failure shapes include `403` cross-origin POST blocked, `401` bad token, `503` extension not connected

## Actions

One JSON `POST /command` surface for 30+ browser actions — page reads and JS (`evaluate`, `cdp`), navigation and tabs (`navigate`, `tabs_list`, `tabs_open`, `find_tab`, ...), interaction (`click`, `fill`, `snapshot`, `type_text`, `send_key`, `mouse_click`, `upload`), capture (`screenshot`, `save_as_pdf`), and native dialogs (`handle_dialog`, `set_dialog_policy`). The full list, one curl per action, is in `docs/HTTP_API.md`.

## MCP

A thin stdio MCP server in `mcp/` exposes five tools — `wf_evaluate`, `wf_cdp`, `wf_navigate`, `wf_tabs_list`, `wf_tabs_activate`; register it per client as described in `docs/MCP.md`.

## Limits

- Drives one tab at a time and never steals your cursor or focus.
- `chrome://`-type pages, the stores and new-tab pages cannot be debugged.
- An open DevTools (or another CDP client) on that tab blocks the bridge.
- On the Firefox edition `navigator.webdriver` is true and cannot be turned off.
- It drives your own logged-in sites; it does not promise anti-bot evasion.
